summary: Wooden tower on Island No. 10 off Shaganash Island, Lake Superior, near Thunder Bay: built 1910, burned 1921, rebuilt 1922-23, staffing ended 1954, heritage 2023.

structures.note: Present tower. Parks Canada, the Register and CLLS say 1922; the Department's report for 1923-24 records the new tower and dwelling built 10 July to 7 Nov 1923.
Separate rectangular dwelling built a short distance from the tower, replacing the combined building (LF; 1923-24 report).
Square wooden dwelling with hipped roof under a square wooden lantern, built by day labour; burned 30 Nov 1921 (LF; report 1921-22).

staffing.note: Staffed until 1954, when the hand foghorn was discontinued and the light changed from fixed to flashing white (LF). CLLS: automated in 1954.

access.note: Reached by boat (LF). Interior of the tower available to tour only when CLLS staff or volunteers are present (CLLS).

facts.agency: Canadian Lighthouses of Lake Superior (non-profit; owner since 2023, per CLLS). Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights: 'Private aid'.

events.note: Built by day labour at a cost of $2,484.90 (LF). Parks Canada: established 1910.
Alexander Clark, the first keeper (LF; Department keeper table for 1911).
Hand-operated foghorn given to the keeper on 10 June 1912 (LF).
Original lighthouse burned down on 30 Nov 1921 (Department report for 1921-22; LF; CLLS).
US Lake Survey notice of 23 Mar 1922: a temporary fixed white oil light shown from a lantern on a pole until further notice (LF).
Present tower dated 1922 by Parks Canada, the Register and CLLS. The Department's report dates the work to 1923 (see the rebuilt entry).
New tower and keeper's dwelling built 10 July to 7 Nov 1923 (Department report for 1923-24).
Staffing ended; hand foghorn discontinued; light changed to flashing white (LF). CLLS: automated in 1954.
Transferred to Canadian Lighthouses of Lake Superior (LF). CLLS: took ownership as a surplus light.
Designated under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act; announced 14 Dec 2023 (Parks Canada).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1910 date belongs to the first tower, which burned on 30 Nov 1921 (Department report for 1921-22; LF). The present tower is dated 1922 by Parks Canada, the Register and CLLS, and the Department's report puts the new tower and dwelling in 10 July to 7 Nov 1923. The 1922/1923 difference is not resolved; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Fact-checked 2026-10-27. Changed: 'Thunder Bay District' removed from the opening (the station record gives it as the county, but no cited source does; 'near Thunder Bay, Ontario' is cited to the Parks backgrounder); 'under new aids to navigation' removed (the 1911 report's heading is not verified); 'The island is reached by boat' changed to Lighthouse Friends' 'best seen by boat'; the keeper-table line is paraphrased because the printed line is an OCR table row (corpus page p. 248, read by row order), so the story no longer quotes it and the page image was not viewed; 1923-24 staffing line now has a footnote; 'a run of short postings' replaced with the LF list as printed. Present tower date disputed: 1922 (Parks Canada, Register, CLLS) against 10 July to 7 Nov 1923 (Department report FY 1923-24, p. 94). Both are in the story. The 1921 fire date is from the report for FY 1921-22 (printed p. 90, 'On November 30 Shaganash lighthouse was burned down'; the year follows from the fiscal year) and from Lighthouse Friends. The keeper table entry 'Alex. Clark' (1911) was read from OCR row order; the row is at printed p. 248, not checked against the page image. The Spears (1913) passage is second-hand from Lighthouse Friends; the book was not read. Keeper Fairall's death date rests on Lighthouse Friends alone. The record's CCG list number 1127 matches the Coast Guard list entry. Chronicling America search for 'Shaganash' 1910-1925 returned nothing; no wreck or rescue tied to the station was found. Peter Belanger (from 1943) is named only as Lighthouse Friends prints him, with no end date and no further detail.
